claims.text: Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 has significant porosity and insufficient mechanical strength for long-term liquid plating-bath exposure.
Adding a minor amount of Si to ZrB2 powder will act as a sintering aid.
Si addition will enable ZrB2 to be sintered at approximately 2000–2100 °C.
Si forms a transient liquid phase during ZrB2 sintering.
The proposed transient Si-rich liquid promotes particle rearrangement and densification.
The Si additive lowers the activation energy for ZrB2 densification.
Si-rich material subsequently segregates to ZrB2 grain boundaries.
Residual Si-rich grain-boundary phases strengthen the microstructure.
Si-rich grain-boundary material forms a protective intergranular barrier.
The proposed intergranular barrier reduces penetration of a liquid plating bath into ZrB2.
Reduced liquid infiltration will reduce pore or hole formation and eventual component failure during plating-bath exposure.
Si-doped ZrB2 will have higher density and lower porosity than conventional ZrB2.
Si-doped ZrB2 will retain phase purity similar to conventional single-phase ZrB2.
Si addition will reduce the required sintering temperature by approximately 200–300 °C.
The lower-temperature Si-assisted process will improve structural integrity.
The Si-assisted material will resist degradation during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure better than conventional ZrB2.
Excess or poorly controlled Si may produce unwanted secondary phases.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis invokes residual Si-rich grain-boundary phases, while also predicting phase purity similar to single-phase ZrB2 and treating secondary-phase formation as a falsifying result. It does not distinguish acceptable segregation or an amorphous film from a disallowed secondary phase.

The stated conventional baseline is ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C, but the proposed comparison sinters both doped and undoped specimens at approximately 2050 °C. Thus, the control does not directly test performance against the defined conventionally prepared baseline.
